draft.title: Technology in sport
card: Technology in sport includes equipment, data and video review. Each can help athletes perform better or help officials make fairer decisions.
gear such as lighter bikes, grippier shoes or better swimwear. It can improve performance, but the best gear often costs more.
wearable trackers record things like heart rate and distance, so coaches can plan training. Video review lets officials check a close call again, which can make decisions fairer.
Technology also raises questions. Athletes or clubs that can afford it may gain an advantage over those who cannot, so some sports set rules on what is allowed.
draft.remember: Technology can lift performance and fairness, but cost can create an unfair advantage.

a.q: Which is a fairness benefit of video review in sport?
opts: Officials can recheck a close call before a final decision
Players no longer need to train with heart rate data
Every club gets the same equipment at the same cost
Umpires are removed from the game completely
a.why: Video review lets officials look again at a close call, which can make the decision fairer. It does not replace training data or umpires, and it does not make equipment cost the same for every club.
a.clue: Think about what officials can do with replays.

b.q: Two rival netball clubs in Bendigo play each other. Only one can afford wearable trackers and video analysis for every player. What question does this raise?
opts: Whether the club's spending gives it an unfair advantage
Whether trackers make heart rate data impossible to read
Whether video review is only used by country clubs
Whether the other club's players must stop training
b.why: Technology can improve performance, but it costs money. A club that can afford more may gain an advantage over one that cannot, which raises a question about fairness. The other options describe things the card does not say technology does.
b.clue: Think about what happens when only one side can pay for the technology.

a.best: Officials can recheck a close call before a final decision

b.best: Whether the club's spending gives it an unfair advantage

proposal.title: Technology in sport
card: Technology in sport includes equipment, data and video review. Each can help athletes perform better or help officials make fairer decisions.
gear such as lighter bikes, grippier shoes or better swimwear. It can improve performance, but the best gear often costs more.
wearable trackers record things like heart rate and distance, so coaches can plan training. Video review lets officials check a close call again, which can make decisions fairer.
Technology also raises questions. Athletes or clubs that can afford it may gain an advantage over those who cannot, so some sports set rules on what is allowed.
proposal.remember: Technology can lift performance and fairness, but cost can create an unfair advantage.

a.q: How does video review help make sport fairer?
opts: A close call can be looked at again before it is decided
Coaches can track each player's heart rate and distance
Athletes can perform better with lighter, grippier gear
Poorer clubs can buy the same gear as their richer rivals
a.why: Video review lets officials look at a close call again, so the decision is more likely to be right and fair. Tracking heart rate and distance is a real use of technology, but it helps coaches plan training, not officials make fair calls.
a.clue: Fairness here is about getting the decision right.

b.q: Two netball clubs in Bendigo are rivals. Only one can afford wearable trackers and video analysis for every player. What concern does this raise?
opts: The richer club may gain an advantage from its spending
Video review may make the umpires' calls less fair
The data may make it harder for coaches to plan training
The trackers may lower each player's performance
b.why: Technology can improve performance, but it costs money, so a club that can pay for more of it may gain an advantage over one that cannot. Video review by officials is meant to make calls fairer, and it is not what this situation is about: the issue is unequal access caused by cost.
b.clue: Focus on what is different between the two clubs.
